(1) the Sun’s corotating interaction region (CIR) is a significant source of the observed interplanetary magnetic field (IMF) at 1 AU during solar minimum, and (2) the Sun’s coronal holes (CHs) are a significant source of open magnetic field at 1 AU, but only during solar maximum.

(1) the Sun’s corotating interaction region (CIR) during the later part of the Maumer Minimum was likely substantially weaker and smaller in size than during the 2008–2009 solar minimum; (2) this CIR was likely driven by the Sun’s ephemeral field; (3) the solar corona during the later part Maunder Minimum had a structure that is similar to that of the solar corona in 2008–2010, but

the Maunder minimum was likely characterized by a coronal structure that was substantially different from the present-day corona, and that the corona evolved from an 11-yr-like structure to an ephemeral-only one during the Maunder epoch, with the corona at the end of the Mauder epoch being similar to what was predicted by our simulations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the nature of the Sun’s magnetic field, and the effects it has on the solar atmosphere, and the surrounding heliosphere.
the structure and dynamics of the solar corona and the inner heliosphere.

understanding how the Sun’s cor- onal magnetic field and solar wind are generated by the Sun’s internal dynamo, how they are affected by the solar wind’s interaction with the interplanetary magnetic field, and how they are affected and modified by the solar wind interaction with the Earth’s magnetic field.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Sun’s corotating interaction region, heliospheric current sheet, and heliospheric magnetic field were all likely significantly reduced or non-existent during the Maunder minimum.

the corona of the Sun during the Maunder minimum was substantially different from its present configuration, and that this difference is consistent with the absence of large-scale magnetic structures, the presence of only ephemeral magnetic structures, and the absence of a global solar wind.
, at least during the latter portion of the Mauder Minimum, the solar corona was likely substantially reduced in size, and devoid of large-scale structure, and driven by only ephemeral regions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have constructed a possible solar minimum state that is consistent with the limited observations from the Maunder epoch, and that we predict a return to a similar state within a few decades.

we have shown that the Sun’s coronal magnetic field during the Maunder minimum was substantially weaker than it is today, and the corona was likely composed of a collection of small-scale structures with no large-scale structure.

the Sun’s coronal and heliospheric structure during the Maunder minimum was substantially different from the modern Sun and that the Maunder and Dalton minima may be the first of a new grand cycle of minima.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the solar corona and inner heliosphere can be very different than what we are accustomed to, and that the Maunder and other grand solar minima may be more extreme than we have previously imagined.
the Sun can exist in a variety of coronal states, some of which may be very different from what we are accustomed to.
, while the solar cycle is a robust phenomenon, the Sun can be, and likely has been, in a state of low activity that is significantly different from that of the modern epoch.
